name: Ethiopian Citizenship by Naturalisation (Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003)

requirements.blocker_text: 4 years of total domicile in Ethiopia -- a notably short period by global standards.
Proficiency in any one of Ethiopia's national/nationality languages -- the 2003 law replaced an older Amharic-only requirement with this broader standard.
requirements.fix_path: Demonstrate proficiency in a qualifying language.

requirements.blocker_text: Must show release from prior nationality, or be stateless -- Ethiopia does not permit dual citizenship.

evidence_required.document: Proof of release from prior nationality
Proof of lawful income sufficient for self and dependents

sources.title: African Child Policy Forum (hosting the full text) -- Ethiopian Nationality Proclamation No. 378/2003: 4-year domicile requirement, language proficiency in any national/nationality language, lawful income sufficiency, good character, no disqualifying criminal record, release from prior nationality or statelessness required

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ethiopia). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a third-party legal-archive hosting of the primary statute (treated as tier 2, consistent with this dataset's convention for research/archive hosts of verbatim government legal text). Ethiopia's justice.gov.et legislation portal was checked but did not yield extractable substantive text in this build -- recommend a follow-up direct fetch before upgrading to published. DISTINCTIVE FINDING: a 4-year residence requirement is notably SHORT by the standards of this dataset -- contrast with Bahrain's 15/25-year tiers, Qatar's 25-year rule, or Rwanda's 15/25-year dual-ground system built elsewhere. MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING: Ethiopia does NOT permit dual citizenship -- voluntarily acquiring a foreign nationality is deemed automatic renunciation of Ethiopian citizenship (a narrow exception exists for nationality acquired involuntarily 'by operation of law,' e.g. automatically at birth, which carries a 1-year-after-adulthood window to formally elect to keep Ethiopian nationality by renouncing the other). This is the exact rationale behind et_ancestry_origin_id.json (the Yellow Card) existing as a diaspora workaround. As of this build's research date, dual-citizenship reform is a live ADVOCACY topic (op-eds and think-tank policy briefs arguing the constitution doesn't itself bar it) but NO enacted legal reform was found -- flagged as active debate, not confirmed law change.
